newsitem.title: USA: New Miami airport delayed for more impact studies.
newsitem.headline: New Miami airport delayed for more impact studies.

text.p: Environmentalists won a partial victory Friday in their effort to get further study of the environmental impact a new Miami airport will have on the Everglades and Biscayne Bay.
The White House announced Friday that it would delay a full transfer of the Homestead Air Reserve Base to developers pending further environmental study.

"We are glad that they recognize that further environmental review is necessary, however, we are disappointed that they are not committed to a supplemental evironmental impact statement," Sarah Chasis, a lawyer for the New York based Natural Resources Defense Council said.
Kathleen McGinty, chairwoman of the White House Council on Environmental Qaulity, outlined the decision Friday at a meeting of the Everglades Coation in Deerfield Beach, Florida, Chasis said.

The Clinton Administration said it "will look at the issue over the next four to ten months," Chasis said. The environmentalists threatened to sue unless a full supplemental environmental impact statement was done.

But the government will allow the development of a smaller scale airport, Chasis said. "We have problems with this segmented approach. It is inevitable that there will be an expansion push," she said.
A lawsuit is "still a possibility," Chasis said.
A spokesman for the developers said Friday they had not yet received notification from the government. "We do not know the scope of the review," said Miguel de Grandy, an attorney.

In January 1996 Dade County officials voted to transfer a long-term lease to the Homestead Air Reserve Base Developers Inc. so they could turn the 1,360 acres into another cargo and passenger airport for the Miami area.
But environmentalists said the development could harm the environmentally fragile Biscayne Bay and the Everglades.
The Miami International Airport, located near downtown Miami, has been struggling to keep up with double-digit growth of passenger and cargo traffic.
